title: Has anyone tried local llm like Ollama for 3D asset generation ?
author: Ok-Branch-2485
selftext: I want to use a local llm for 3d asset generation. Claude and blender MCP uses a lot of tokens

comments.author: Charming_You_25
comments.body: Yes but the best ones are only decent for high poly models and getting them down is janky. Paid ones like triplo are still best

comments.author: Toastti
comments.body:
Yes and it works decent IF you are able to run a model such as Qwen 3.8 27b. Which requires a 3090 at minimum basically. 

There is very little point spending time on testing this with your 5060 unfortunately. It just has too little vram to run any model actually capable of 3d model creation. 

If you do still want to try Qwen 3.5 35b is your best bet if you have enough ram. It will run decent on your machine and can sorta do basic models with blender mcp

comments.author: Three_Tails_Studio
comments.body: 8GB isn’t nearly enough … will take days to perform simple tasks.

comments.author: robobax
comments.body: you’re better off using comfy ui and a local 3d workflow. Plenty of tutorials on how to set that up on youtube.

comments.author: ludoaiplatform
comments.body:
Worth separating two things: Ollama runs text LLMs, so with Blender MCP it would only replace Claude as the thing writing Blender Python. That works, but small local models are much worse at long tool-calling chains, so expect more broken scripts. The geometry still comes from bpy code either way.

If what you actually want is meshes, look at dedicated image-to-3D models instead. Most of them run through ComfyUI wrappers:

\- TripoSR and Stable Fast 3D: light, fit comfortably in 8GB, quick. Fine for props and blockout, rougher on characters.

\- Hunyuan3D-2 mini: better shapes, runs on 8GB with the low-VRAM settings. The texturing stage is the heavier part, so you may have to do shape only and texture separately.

\- TRELLIS: good results, but you'll be fighting 8GB.

The typical local flow is: generate a clean front-view image (plain background, neutral pose) → image-to-3D → bring the mesh into Blender for cleanup/decimation. At that point you can use an LLM for the small scripted steps, which costs far fewer tokens than having it model from scratch.

comments.author: DaedalusRaistlin
comments.body:
I use Trellis2, the 8Gb fork of it, and generate models on my 3060 Ti 8Gb. Works alright, the problem is reducing it to game ready polygon counts. The retopology approaches I've tried so far haven't worked very well. The textures also don't come out very well, but that's a different step and there are few different options I'm exploring - nothing concrete yet.

/r/TopologyAI has some promising leads I haven't tried yet for the texturing stage, and I want to explore some of the other (non Trellis) models too.
